situation:
You are a recent graduate, three months into your first salaried job, and you have just signed a lease on an apartment. An insurance agent (judge) at HARLOW RIDGE INSURANCE, who wrote the liability coverage on your car, has agreed to meet you and hear how you plan to replace your phone.

You dropped the phone and the screen cracked. RIVERGLASS MOBILE offers two ways to replace it. An installment plan spreads the full price over twenty-four months and leaves you owning the phone at the end. An upgrade lease costs less each month, but you must return the phone after twenty-four months and carry device protection every month you hold it.

Buying on the installment plan means the phone is yours and you skip the monthly protection charge. It also means that if you crack a screen again, you pay the full repair price yourself, out of the same paycheck that already covers rent and your auto premium.

Taking the upgrade lease keeps the monthly payment low and puts a covered replacement in your hand the day something happens. You hand the phone back after twenty-four months owning nothing, and two years of protection payments return nothing if the phone is never damaged.

The agent (judge) wants you to compare what each course costs, recommend one, and explain how you would carry the choice out, using the same reasoning that set the deductible on your health plan. The agent (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after you have presented and answered the questions.
